solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Chart second half of photo

indicators.note: only the back half of the full word is kept, so its front half is dropped

parts.note: photo is the short form of photograph

explanation.surface: Someone is told to chart the latter part of a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'photo' stands for the full word photograph; 'second half of' keeps only its last five letters, dropping PHOTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A graph is a diagram plotting data, which is what a chart is.

clue.text: Track British-American coach

parts.note: a rail is a track for trains
US means American

explanation.surface: A transatlantic coach company runs on track.
explanation.definitionFit: A railbus is a light passenger rail vehicle resembling a bus, so a kind of coach on rails.

clue.text: Dad's holiday?

parts.note: a father's time off work, read as the leave granted on the birth of a child

explanation.surface: Someone wonders where Father is going for his break.
explanation.definitionFit: Paternity leave is time off work granted to a father around his child's birth.

clue.text: I am past the adult stage

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
ago means in the past, as in two years ago

explanation.surface: Someone sadly admits they are now beyond adulthood.
explanation.definitionFit: In entomology the imago is the final, fully grown stage of an insect after metamorphosis.

clue.text: Bird's short time with another heron

parts.note: mo is short for moment

indicators.note: another version of the word heron, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird spends a brief spell with a second heron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' looks like it wants a second bird, but it signals a fresh arrangement of the heron's letters; 'short time' is the familiar 'half a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: A moorhen is a common water bird of the rail family.

clue.text: Talk covering healthier worker in a fuel industry

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece sits on top of the other, covering it

parts.note: gas is idle chatter
fitter means healthier

explanation.surface: Chatter conceals a fitter employee at an energy firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas fitter installs and repairs gas appliances and pipes, working in the gas trade.

clue.text: One is stupid to continue

explanation.surface: A dim person is urged to carry on.
explanation.definitionFit: A goon is a foolish person, and go on means carry on.

clue.text: People with pride sit fidgeting showing unselfish interest

parts.note: the public are people at large

indicators.note: fidgeting means moving restlessly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Proud citizens squirm while showing concern for others.
explanation.definitionFit: Being public-spirited means acting for the good of the community rather than oneself.

clue.text: Third degree sunburn?

parts.note: a severe burn on the surface, but meaning the third-placed medal and a deep tan colour

explanation.surface: A doctor queries a severe case of sunburn.
explanation.definitionFit: Bronze is the third-place medal and also the brown colour of tanned skin.

clue.text: Very riotous sort of person who is highly skilled

indicators.note: sort of suggests a loose version, so the letters of riotous are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wild, rowdy character turns out to be remarkably talented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very riotous' reads as a description of the person, but 'Very' is just its abbreviation and 'sort of' scrambles the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: A virtuoso is a performer of exceptional technical skill, especially a musician.

clue.text: Unimportant person coming from jet

explanation.surface: A nobody emerges from a spray of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally an insignificant person is a squirt, and a squirt is also a thin jet of liquid.

clue.text: King from Borneo

indicators.note: from here signals letters made out of the following word, rearranged

explanation.surface: A monarch hails from the island of Borneo.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon is king of the fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Crack above the forehead

explanation.surface: A fracture sits just over someone's brow.
explanation.definitionFit: A very thin crack is called a hairline fracture, and the edge of the hair growth above the brow is the hairline.

clue.text: Saint not going beyond another saint

parts.note: within means inside limits, not exceeding them

explanation.surface: One saint stays within the bounds of another.
explanation.definitionFit: St Swithin is an English saint whose feast day, 15 July, is linked to rain folklore.

clue.text: Agatha's man linked to article of extraordinary power

parts.note: Hercule Poirot is Agatha Christie's detective
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Agatha Christie's sleuth is connected to an object of immense strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Herculean describes strength or effort worthy of the mythical hero Hercules.

clue.text: Australian food from school shop about to be returned

parts.note: a tuck shop sells snacks at British schools, so tuck is the school shop's name

indicators.note: returned means the word for about is read backwards

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Australian grub is bought at the school shop and then sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: A tuck shop is a British school snack shop, so 'school shop' supplies only its first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tucker is Australian slang for food or grub.

clue.text: Not a goer in the race?

definitions.text: Not a goer in the race?

parts.words: Not a goer in the race?
parts.note: reads as a non-runner, but means a horse or runner built for long distances, one that keeps going

explanation.surface: Someone asks who is not taking part in the race.
explanation.definitionFit: A stayer is a horse or athlete with stamina for long races, punningly one who 'stays' rather than goes.

clue.text: Upsetting experience in Sumatra strangely headed off

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd order, so the letters are rearranged
the head, or first letter, of the word is removed

explanation.surface: A distressing event happens in Sumatra, oddly cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headed off' drops S from SUMATRA to leave UMATRA, which 'strangely' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A trauma is a deeply distressing or disturbing experience.

clue.text: Monkey appearing in section of wall

indicators.note: appearing in means one piece shows up inside another

parts.note: part means a section
an ape is a monkey-like primate, loosely a monkey

explanation.surface: A monkey turns up on a stretch of wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is a low protective wall along the edge of a roof, bridge or balcony.

clue.text: Before wise man reveals foreboding

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before
a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: In advance, a sage discloses a sense of doom.
explanation.definitionFit: A presage is an omen or feeling that something will happen, a foreboding.

clue.text: Look-alike arranged matching clothes

parts.note: a twin is someone who looks alike
set means arranged, put in order

explanation.surface: A double lays out a coordinated outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinset is a woman's matching cardigan and jumper worn together.

clue.text: Be certain to do this

parts.note: an instruction to confirm something, which is itself the phrase meaning to check or ensure

explanation.surface: A reminder to be sure to get a task done.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure or verify something is to be certain of it, the sense of the phrasal verb asked for here.

clue.text: Singular physical exercise in short coat

parts.note: a jerk is a single lift in weightlifting, as in clean and jerk

explanation.surface: A lone workout is done wearing a short coat.
explanation.walkthrough: The jerk is the second movement of the weightlifter's clean and jerk.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerkin is a sleeveless close-fitting jacket, historically of leather.

clue.text: Bird to suffer after beginning of July

indicators.note: after places the ailment word behind the July letter
beginning of picks out the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: ail means to suffer or be ill

explanation.surface: A bird starts to suffer at the start of July.
explanation.walkthrough: Bird is slang for a prison sentence, or prison itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Bird is British slang for a stretch in prison, so a jail.

clue.text: Second turn I included might be screened

parts.note: B is second in the alphabet, a second-rate grade

indicators.note: included means one piece is placed within another

parts.note: a move is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: A second go in which I take part could be shown.
explanation.definitionFit: A B-movie is a low-budget film, something that would be shown in a cinema.

clue.text: Searching examination, it's acted out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A searching test comes, for it has been acted out.
explanation.definitionFit: An acid test is a decisive trial of worth, from testing gold with nitric acid.

clue.text: Reference section on hand

explanation.surface: A part of a reference book is readily available.
explanation.definitionFit: A book's index is its alphabetical reference section, and the index finger is a digit on the hand.

clue.text: Letters of credit helped the lady

indicators.note: letters of means a run of letters taken from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Letters of credit assisted a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith is a woman's name, and a female name can stand for 'the lady'.
